Supreme Court of India

5 April 2006
Appeal (Cr.) 779 of 2005
The Judgment was delivered by: S. B. Sinha, J
1.  Davamani (the deceased) was the wife of the appellant herein. She admittedly committed suicide on 14.03.1994. They were married on 04.09.1992. The deceased gave birth to a female child at Pondicherry in July 1993. The appellant for one reason or the other did not bring her back from her maternal home for a period of about eight months. She was brought back in February 1994. According to the appellant, the deceased proposed to go back to her mother's house to see her mother which he refused stating that she had come back only a month back.
2. It is not in dispute that at the time when the deceased committed suicide neither the appellant nor his mother was present in the house. Somehow or the other the people of the neighbourhood came to know about it. They broke open the door and found the dead body. The deceased committed suicide at about 1 p.m.. Th
facts: The wife of the appellant, Davamani, committed suicide on 14.03.1994.
The couple got married on 04.09.1992 and had a child in July 1993.
The deceased stayed with her husband for about seven months before going back to her mother's place for delivery of the child.
The incident took place on 14.03.1994, when the deceased committed suicide.
A case under Section 304B of the Indian Penal Code was registered against the appellant alone.
An investigation into the offence was carried out by a Superintendent of Police and an enquiry was conducted by a Deputy Tahsildar-cum-Executive Magistrate.
issues: Whether the demand of dowry was made by the accused party or not?
Whether the death of the deceased was caused by harassment for demand of dowry or not?
petitioner_arguments: The appellant argued that there was no evidence to prove that he had demanded dowry from his wife.
He also argued that the witnesses who supported the prosecution's case were unreliable.
respondent_arguments: The respondent argued that the deceased had been harassed for demand of dowry and that the appellant was responsible for her death.
court_reasoning: The court held that the evidence led by the prosecution failed to establish involvement of the Appellant as regards the alleged demand of dowry.
It also held that the witnesses who supported the prosecution's case were unreliable.
holding: The court acquitted the appellant, holding that there was no sufficient evidence to prove his guilt.
